sections.h2: How big is Meridian and where does it sit?
sections.html:
Meridian is the second most populous city in Idaho, after Boise, and it is in Ada County. The Census Bureau estimates 142,988 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 117,635 at the 2020 census. Wikipedia describes it as the state's fastest-growing city.

The city covers about 26.8 square miles on a flat plain in the north central part of the Treasure Valley. Boise lies to the east and Nampa to the west, and the Boise River runs north of the city. The Owyhee Mountains are visible far to the south.

Because the city is so large, a Meridian house can compete with a very deep pool of listings, including many new builds. That depth is the main reason sellers with repair needs or a short timeline look at options besides a standard listing.

sections.h2: What is the history of Meridian?
sections.html:
Meridian grew from an irrigated farm community. The town was first called Hunter in 1891, then renamed Meridian after an I.O.O.F. lodge noted it sat on the Boise Meridian. The original townsite was filed in 1893.

Irrigation made farming possible, since receiving a land patent required a water source. The Nampa-Meridian and Settlers irrigation districts still serve the area, and several canals cross the city from southeast to northwest. Around 1900 settlers planted orchards and built fruit packing businesses and prune dryers along the rail line. Production continued until the mid-1940s.

  • 1900: Union Pacific spur opened, now operated by the Boise Valley Railroad.
  • 1908 to 1928: an interurban rail line connected Meridian to Boise and Nampa.
  • 1929 to 1970: the Ada County Dairymen's cooperative creamery operated, producing Challenge Butter.

That farm and canal history is still visible in lot lines and irrigation easements. When you sell, ask whether your lot has pressurized irrigation or a ditch right so you can answer a buyer's question.

sections.h2: Which employers and roads define Meridian?
sections.html:
Meridian is the home of Blue Cross of Idaho, Jacksons Food Stores and Scentsy. The Idaho State Police is headquartered in Meridian, and its academy trains all police officers in the state. The Village at Meridian, a retail and restaurant district, opened in 2013.

The street grid is easy to read. Most of the city lies north of I-84, and street names carry a north, south, east or west prefix relative to the intersection of Franklin Road and Meridian Road. From west to east the major roads are Black Cat, Ten Mile, Linder, Meridian, Locust Grove and Eagle. From north to south they are Chinden (Highway 20/26), McMillan, Ustick, Cherry or Fairview, Franklin, Overland, Victory and Amity.

Old Town Meridian centers on Main Street and Pine Street. Most industrial areas run along the railroad line between Pine and Franklin. Buyers often shop by the nearest major intersection, so use those cross streets in a listing or when describing your house to a cash buyer.

sections.h2: What is the Meridian climate and how does it affect a house?
sections.html:
Meridian has a semi-arid climate with four distinct seasons, hot dry summers and cold winters with occasional light snow. Summer cooling and irrigation matter more than winter loads.

MeasureMeridian
Record high111 F (July)
Wettest monthDecember, 1.55 inches
Driest monthAugust, 0.24 inches
Typical monthly rainfallUsually under one inch

Summer temperatures can often exceed 100 F. A buyer's inspector will look at the age of the air conditioner, attic insulation and ventilation, window condition and sprinkler system. Replacing a failed cooling unit before a sale can cost real money, and a cash buyer will account for it in the price instead of requiring you to fix it first.

sections.h2: How do permits and building rules work in Meridian?
sections.html:
Meridian's Building Services handles permits for structural, fire, electrical, mechanical and plumbing work for residential, commercial and industrial projects. The office is at 33 E. Broadway Ave. #102, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, phone 208-887-2211.

Services include permit application, plan review, permit issuance and field inspection. Other permits cover remodels, mobile homes, fences, sheds, garages, foundations, fireplaces and demolition. Applications, fee payment and inspection scheduling run through the online citizen portal, and a certificate of occupancy is issued after all required inspections are complete.

The City Council meets on the first through fourth Tuesdays of the month, with a work session at 4:30 p.m. and public hearings at 6:00 p.m. Planning and Zoning decisions affect nearby development, so a seller next to vacant land can check the city's hearing agendas.

  • Look up permit history before listing, especially for garages, sheds and remodels.
  • Close out open permits if you can, since an open permit can delay a closing.
  • Keep final inspection records with your other home documents.

The West Ada School District serves almost all of Meridian and is the largest district in Idaho. A portion of Meridian extends into the Kuna Joint School District 3.

That split matters when a buyer asks which schools serve your address. Confirm boundaries with the district rather than assuming them from the city name. Property tax bills also include school district levies, so the district shown on your bill is a quick way to check.

sections.h2: How are Meridian property taxes billed and due?
sections.html:
Ada County bills property tax for Meridian. The full-year primary roll payment or first half is due December 20, and the second half is due June 20 if the first half is paid on time.

DateEvent (Ada County)
January 1Appraisers set market value; first day to apply for homeowner's exemption
First Monday in JuneAssessment notices mailed
June 20Second half due
Fourth Monday in JuneLast day to appeal a value
Fourth Monday in NovemberPrimary roll bills mailed (by this date)
December 20Full-year payment or first half due

If the 20th falls on a weekend or holiday, a payment postmarked on or before the 20th counts as timely the next business day. Ada County also issues subsequent and missed roll bills for improvements and later-assessed property, due June 20. Sellers of recently built or remodeled houses should ask the title company to look for those.

The Idaho State Tax Commission says the homeowner's exemption covers 50% of the value of an owner-occupied primary home and up to one acre, with a $125,000 maximum, and that it lasts until ownership changes. Idaho law does not cap changes in value, and each taxing district can raise the property tax part of its budget by no more than 3% unless voters approve more or new construction and annexation add to the base. For questions, email taxinfo@adacounty.id.gov or call 208-287-6800.

sections.h2: What must a Meridian seller disclose under Idaho law?
sections.html:
Idaho Code 55-2504 requires a person transferring one to four unit residential property to complete a property condition disclosure form, including nonowner-occupied rentals. It covers sales, exchanges, installment contracts and options.

Idaho Code 55-2505 exempts several transfers, such as foreclosure transfers, estate transfers by a fiduciary, transfers to a spouse or lineal relative, and newly built homes never lived in, though those sellers must still declare annexation and city service status. A Meridian owner who is unsure should ask an Idaho attorney or title officer.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work for a Meridian house?
sections.html:
A cash sale removes the lender, so your timeline depends on title work and the closing date you pick. You request an offer, the buyer looks at the house, and a title company closes and pays off any mortgage or taxes from proceeds.

  • Share occupancy, liens, back taxes and needed repairs up front.
  • Compare the offer with listing costs, repair estimates and holding costs.

You owe nothing if you turn an offer down. In a market as large as Meridian, a listing may suit a house in good condition, so a local agent's opinion is a useful comparison.

faqs.q: How many people live in Meridian, Idaho?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 142,988 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 117,635, making Meridian the second most populous city in the state.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax in Meridian?
faqs.a: Ada County does. The full-year or first-half payment is due December 20, and the second half is due June 20 if the first half was paid on time.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Meridian property value?
faqs.a: The last day to submit an appeal is the fourth Monday in June. Assessment notices from the Ada County Assessor go out the first Monday in June.

faqs.q: Where do I get a building permit record in Meridian?
faqs.a: Contact Meridian Building Services at 33 E. Broadway Ave. #102, phone 208-887-2211, or use the city's online citizen portal to track permits and inspections.

faqs.q: Which school district is Meridian in?
faqs.a: Most of Meridian is in the West Ada School District, the largest in Idaho. A portion of the city extends into the Kuna Joint School District 3.

faqs.q: Does the buyer inherit my homeowner's exemption?
faqs.a: No. The exemption ends when ownership changes, so the buyer applies with the county assessor if they will live in the home as their primary residence.
